To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new method to measure the amplitude of the stellar oscillations, and that we have developed new observational strategies to average out the stellar noise and to detect Earth-like planets in the habitables zone of solar type stars.
we have developed a new strategy for the detection of Earth-like planets around stars like the sun, which is based on the use of a new generation of spectrographs.

we have developed a model that allows us to predict the RV variations induced by stellar noise (oscillations, granulations, and activity) on solar type stars, and that we have demonstrated that it is possible to average out simultaneously all type(s) of noise with a specific observational strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study and characterization of the different types of stellar noise, in order to find the best observational strategy to detect the Earth-like planets.

3 aspects: - the stellar physics, to better understand and model the stellar noise coming from oscillation, granulation and activity - the instrumental physics, to improve the instrumental precision, to better model the instrumental noise and to better model and correct the stellar noise - the observational strategy, to optimize the observational strategy to average out the stellar noise and the instrumental noise.

- the study of the impact of stellar noise on the RV precision and planet detection - the development of a new observational strategy, optimized to reduce the stellar noise, and the development of the required data reduction software - the study of new instrumental solutions to reduce the stellar and instrumental noise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
- Stellar noise is a major problem for the detection of Earth mass planets in habitable zone around solar-type stars.
the RV noise is a combination of oscillations, granulations and activity.
the current HARPS strategy is optimal to detect planets around solar-type stars, but not to detect Earth mass planets in habitable zones of solar-type stars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to measure the RV of the Sun with a precision of 0.1 m/s.
the RV variations of the Sun are dominated by granulation, which is the most difficult phenomenon to average out.
we need to understand better the stellar noise to be able to detect Earth-like planets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RV variations induced by stellar noise can be reduced significantly by using the right observational strategy.
the stellar noise is dominated by the granulation phenomena.
the RV precision of HARPS can be improved from 0.5 m/s to 0.1 m/s by using the new strategy we have developed.
